retirement_prerequisites: budget.settle returns exact string settled or duplicate after its own committed readback
implementation.strong_retention: Active, held, failed-publication and uncertain-settlement owners remain in _OWNERS[id(handle)]. No GC, age or PID observation releases authority or refunds budget.
implementation.retired_cache: WeakKeyDictionary exact handle -> {record: detached JSON fullRef/scope/permit/terminal, process: independent weakref to the original process}. Neither record nor process weakref strongly references the key or process. The weakref has no callback.
implementation.identity_correction: The first candidate used a mutable handle._retired_process witness. The final candidate trusts only the independent private cache weakref and compares its referent with handle.process by is; it does not trust the handle-provided weakref or PID/id.
implementation.consumers: Same live terminal handle harvest/stop returns a detached historical terminal. Wrong scope, permit, fullRef, process or fake handle is refused. Cached terminal readback is not permission for new GO, source publication or settlement.
implementation.shared_capture: Retirement drops this owner's admission/domain/action/binding roots, without explicit removal or invalidation of a shared externally held DomainRun or PreparedSources.

final_readonly_review.outcome: No blocking contradiction found in the limited retirement contract.
details: Successful cpu_phase.close alone clears invocation roots and unregisters only its unique exit callback; any native/Lake-close uncertainty retains roots.

Signal restoration occurs only when the current handler is this invocation's exact handler. _ShutdownHandler.predecessor skips retired internal predecessors, and retired handlers drop engine references, so non-LIFO close cannot restore an engine-retaining handler.
Interface weak-value registry captures are held by exact opaque handles and external owners; retirement is not a shared-run invalidation.
No final pass result here proves a general bound on user-held references, interpreter registries, unknown execution, RSS or arbitrary trusted callback behavior.
